doc: Rolls-Royce Holdings plc Form F-6 registration statement (ADR programme), signature page
speaker: Rolls-Royce Holdings plc (signatures of directors)
quote: Anita Frew Chairman of the Board of Directors ... George Culmer Senior Independent Director ... Lord Jitesh Gadhia Independent Non-Executive Director ... Mike Manley Independent Non-Executive Director
finding: On 8 July 2022 the board had 13 directors: Anita Frew as Chairman; two executives (CEO Warren East, CFO Panos Kakoullis); ten independent non-executives (Paul Adams, George Culmer as Senior Independent Director, Lord Jitesh Gadhia, Beverly Goulet, Lee Hsien Yang, Nick Luff, Mike Manley, Wendy Mars, Sir Kevin Smith, Dame Angela Strank). This is the latest full director list in our sources; the chair and CEO roles are split.

doc: Rolls-Royce Holdings plc Form F-6 registration statement (ADR programme), signature page
speaker: Rolls-Royce Holdings plc (signatures of directors)
quote: Sir Ian Davis Chairman of the Board of Directors ... Warren East CBE Chief Executive Officer and Director ... Senior Independent Director Sir Kevin Smith
finding: In February 2021, after the recapitalisation, the board had 13 directors under Chairman Sir Ian Davis, with Sir Kevin Smith as Senior Independent Director and only the CEO and CFO as executives.

speaker: Ian Davis, Chairman
quote: I'm Ian Davis, I'm your Chairman and I'm joined on stage by Warren East, Chief Executive; Stephen Daintith, Chief Financial Officer and the Chairs of our board committees; Ruth Cairnie, Chair of the Remuneration Committee; Lewis Booth, Chair of the Audit committee; Kevin Smith, Chair of Science and Technology Committee and also our Senior Independent Director; and Frank Chapman, Chair of the Safety and Ethics Committee.
finding: The board runs through standing committees beyond the UK-code trio: Remuneration, Audit, a Science and Technology Committee (technology and product oversight) and a Safety and Ethics Committee (later Safety, Ethics and Sustainability).

speaker: Ian Davis, Independent Chairman
quote: She joined us at the start of this month and will be a member of the Nominations and Governance Committee, the Safety, Ethics and Sustainability Committee and The Science and Technology Committee. ... A Chartered Accountant, George, was until recently Chief Financial Officer at Lloyds Banking Group, and is also the Senior Independent Director at Aviva.
finding: Committee names as of 2020: Nominations and Governance; Safety, Ethics and Sustainability; Science and Technology; Audit. Dame Angela Strank (BP chief scientist) and George Culmer (ex-Lloyds CFO) joined, adding science and finance depth.

speaker: Ian Davis, Independent Chairman
quote: Also in 2019, Brad Singer, a Partner and Chief Operating Officer of ValueAct Capital stepped down as a Nonexecutive Director. Since joining us in 2016, Brad had been an active member of the Board, offering a valued external perspective and helping us to drive progress in our efforts to transform Rolls-Royce.
finding: From 2016 to 2019 a partner of the investor ValueAct Capital sat on the board during the East turnaround; the chair credited him with helping drive the transformation. (inference) Investor pressure for returns has reached the boardroom directly.

speaker: Ian Davis, Independent Chairman
quote: However, the Board has approved that he will remain as an independent Nonexecutive Director and as an Audit Committee member, to provide continuity of support to Nick Luff as Nick takes over as Chairman of the Audit Committee. The Board also approved the time extension for Sir Frank Chapman to remain as an independent Nonexecutive Director and as Chairman of The Safety, Ethics and Sustainability Committee, recognizing his significant support for our safety, ethics and sustainability agenda.
finding: In the COVID crisis the board kept Lewis Booth, the Audit Committee chair stepping down after nine years, on the board and the Audit Committee for continuity as Nick Luff (RELX CFO, RG-0046) took the Audit chair, and extended Sir Frank Chapman's tenure as chair of the Safety, Ethics and Sustainability Committee. The board values continuity on safety and audit oversight over strict tenure rules.

speaker: Ian Davis, Independent Chairman
quote: And the Board has extensive experience of engineering as well as technology and indeed as well in the aerospace sector as well, contrary to what you claim. Several of our members on the Board are chartered engineers.
finding: Answering a shareholder who said no director understood the airline industry, the chair defended the board as engineering- and aerospace-literate. The board sees itself as able to judge technical programme risk.

speaker: Warren East, CEO
quote: I'd point out that we also highlight that 3 of our directors are leaving the Board. They're timing out. And so this is part of the normal succession process. Now Paul was Head of Engineering at Pratt & Whitney for some years, and so he clearly has some very relevant industrial experience.
finding: Paul Adams, a former head of engineering at Pratt & Whitney, joined the board in 2021 to replace industrial experience lost as three long-serving directors timed out. A director knows the GTF rival's engineering from inside (relevant to Joint Venture and narrowbody judgements).

speaker: Warren East, CEO
quote: we've also appointed a new chair, Anita Frew, who joined the Board a month ago and will succeed Sir Ian Davis on the 1st of October. Anita is an experienced chair with in-depth experience from 2 decades of Board appointments, both in the U.K. and internationally ... This half, we also appointed Mike Manley as Non-Executive Director, and he joined the Board from the 1st of July.
finding: Anita Frew became Chair on 1 October 2021, succeeding Sir Ian Davis; the CEO described her as an experienced chair with two decades of board appointments in the U.K. and internationally. Mike Manley, who has led automotive businesses in Europe, Asia and the U.S., joined in July 2021.

speaker: Anita Frew, Independent Non-Executive Chairman
quote: You'll have seen our announcement this morning that Warren plans to step down at the end of this year. By then, Warren will have spent 9 years on the Board and almost 8 years as CEO, a relatively long tenure and a tribute to his strength and commitment. As a result, we're now starting an open and transparent search process for Warren's successor.
finding: Under Frew the board ran an 'open and transparent' CEO search in 2022 that produced Tufan Erginbilgic as CEO from January 2023 (RX-0038). (inference) He is not in any earlier RR evidence, so the board looked outside rather than repeating its pattern of promoting a sitting non-executive (Rishton 2011, East 2015).

speaker: Anita Frew, Independent Non-Executive Chairman
quote: In his time at Rolls-Royce, he's created a dramatically different business and has positioned us well to generate substantial value from the drive to net zero. Finally, I would just like to thank Warren on behalf of the whole Board for his tremendous work.
finding: The chair's public framing of strategy in 2022 was long-horizon (value from the energy transition), while the CEO change that followed refocused on near-term profit and cash (R-1561).

speaker: Ian Davis, Chairman
quote: John Rishton is going to be retiring from Rolls-Royce in the summer and that Warren East will take over from him as Chief Executive. This happened after an extensive search once John had told me towards the end of last year of his intentions to retire. ... he does have the advantage knowing a little bit about the company and the company knowing him. And I think that does reduce the cultural risk
finding: In 2015 the board chose a sitting non-executive director (East) as CEO after an extensive search, explicitly to reduce cultural risk; a risk-averse succession choice.

speaker: John Rishton, CEO
quote: I joined the board of Rolls-Royce as a nonexecutive in 2007. I took on the role of CEO in April of this year.
finding: The 2011 CEO was also a former non-executive director; together with East (2015) this shows the pre-2022 board preferring known insiders for the top job.

speaker: Ian Davis, Chairman
quote: Short term, you're right, but longer term, this is a growth story. ... We do recognize, and Warren knows, he doesn't have the manufacturing experience, but there's a lot of that in Rolls-Royce. There's also quite a bit of that on the Board as well.
finding: The chair separates the short-term restructuring task from the long-term growth story, and says the board itself supplies manufacturing expertise to the CEO.

speaker: Ian Davis, Chairman
quote: neither the board nor myself are under any illusions, any illusions at all about how concerned and how frustrated many of you in this room are. We get it. And we get the associated need for decisive but well-judged action. ... the overwhelming priority now is to improve our financial and our operating performance and to increase the speed of response to events and improve our internal controls.
finding: After the 2014-15 profit warnings the board set financial and operating performance and internal controls as the overwhelming priority, ahead of growth bets.

speaker: Ian Davis, Chairman
quote: And I should just say that the profile of appointments to the board reflect these priorities and will continue to do so.
finding: The board shapes its own membership around the current priority (financial and operational repair). (inference) This fits the finance-heavy non-executive bench (Luff, Culmer) that followed.

speaker: Ian Davis, Chairman
quote: Fundamentally, long term this is a growth story. In my and the board's judgment, Warren has got off to a very strong start in challenging circumstances ... he and the management team have the total support of the board in executing these priorities and delivering the value-creation potential in the business.
finding: The board publicly backs its CEO once it has set the priorities; support is conditional on executing the performance plan.

speaker: Ian Davis, Chairman
quote: The overwhelming priority for the company is financial and operational performance improvement. They are very, very closely linked in this company. Finance and operations are the twin pillars. Lots of other things we could be worrying about as a board, but we're not. This is our laserlike focus, financial and operational performance.
finding: In the 2015-18 turnaround the board explicitly narrowed its focus to finance and operations, deprioritising other agenda items.

speaker: Ian Davis, Chairman
quote: Our absolute priority -- our absolute priority -- is to overcome these. Customer trust and confidence has to be our #1 goal. ... Progress will not be smooth, given the nature of the industry and the number of new products we are in the process of introducing into the market. And I do not want to underestimate the risks.
finding: With in-service fleet issues (Trent 1000) and many new engines entering service at once, the chair put customer trust first and warned of the risk of running several new products together.

speaker: Ian Davis, Chairman
quote: We've refreshed our strategy and long-term vision, we've refined our capital allocation process, we've delivered financial results ahead of budget and expectations
finding: The board reports owning the capital allocation process (refined in 2017) as well as strategy.

speaker: Ian Davis, Chairman
quote: We are a long-term business with very long investment cycles. We've continued our commitment to, and investment in, next-generation technologies and facilities that will be crucial to competitiveness and value creation.
finding: The board describes the company as long-cycle and claims to protect next-generation technology spend through short-term pressure (with R-1448).

speaker: Ian Davis, Chairman
quote: the absolute priority of the board is to ensure the financial and operational performance improvement in the company to get to where we can and we should be, but also to ensure that we're making investments in building the organization capacity to position ourselves for the future.
finding: The board balances near-term performance repair with investment for the future; performance comes first in the sentence.

speaker: Ian Davis, Chairman
quote: So the way I think and the board thinks about governance, it is actually a performance tool as well as something that it allows you to fulfill your obligations to society, to investors and your employees
finding: The board treats governance as a performance lever and weighs obligations to society, investors and employees together (UK stakeholder model).

speaker: Lewis Booth, Audit Committee Chair
quote: A key part of the role of the audit committee is to review the judgments made in our long-term contract accounting, particularly in Civil Aerospace. ... we continued to review the risk management process as well as the 3 specific areas of principal risk that are allocated to the Audit Committee, those are business continuity, IT vulnerability and market and financial risks. We believe that the risk management process is being successfully embedded into Rolls-Royce and it's increasingly being factored into the decision-making process.
finding: The Audit Committee reviews long-term contract accounting judgements in Civil and owns named principal risks (business continuity, IT, market and financial); principal risks are allocated to committees and fed into decisions.

speaker: Sir Frank Chapman, Non-Executive Director, Chair of the Safety, Ethics and Sustainability Committee
quote: And one of the topics very close to my heart is safety performance, both in terms of product safety performance and occupational safety performance. This is one of these things if you take your hands off of it, you could end up in the place where you would wish not to be. We have a moral obligation to do these things properly.
finding: A board committee chair owns product and occupational safety oversight and treats it as a moral obligation that needs constant attention.

speaker: Paul Stein, Chief Technology Officer
quote: our group environmental strategy is governed by an Environmental and Sustainability Committee, which we set up internally to provide a focal point for the executive team and that's overseen by the Science and Technology Committee for our products and services and the Safety, Ethics and Sustainability Committees for our operations
finding: Board-level oversight is split: the Science and Technology Committee oversees products and technology (e.g. UltraFan), the Safety, Ethics and Sustainability Committee oversees operations.

speaker: Ian Davis, Chairman
quote: This has been an area of continued and continuing focus and oversight by your Board. And I would like to praise the sterling efforts of our engineering and customer support teams in addressing these issues while maintaining our absolute dedication to ensuring product safety, which is and always must be our most important priority.
finding: The board oversaw the Trent 1000 durability crisis directly and states product safety is always its most important priority.

speaker: Ian Davis, Chairman
quote: It remains our stated objective in the long term to progressively rebuild payments to shareholders to an appropriate level, subject to the cash needs of the business.
finding: Even in recovery the board subordinated shareholder payments to the cash needs of the business (with R-0738).

speaker: Ian Davis, Chairman
quote: Across Rolls-Royce, our immediate focus is on improving our financial and operational performance to generate improved returns. This will give us the sound and credible financial platform we need in order to remain at the cutting edge of innovation in our markets.
finding: The board sequences: returns and a credible financial platform first, then innovation leadership. Long-term technology ambition is funded by, and conditional on, near-term returns.

speaker: Ian Davis, Independent Chairman
quote: Immediately after the conclusion of this meeting, we'll hold a general meeting on a single resolution recommending an increase of our borrowing limits in order to give us greater flexibility at this time. We do not have plans to borrow out of this limit. But in a time of uncertainty, we believe it is prudent to create headroom to give management flexibility to act as necessary. ... Your Board believes that the resolution being proposed at this general meeting is in the best interest of the company and its shareholders as a whole. And the Directors have voted in favor of this resolution.
finding: Borrowing limits are set by shareholders on the board's recommendation; in 2020 the board sought headroom it did not plan to use, a precautionary liquidity move, and the directors voted in favour of the resolution.

speaker: Ian Davis, Independent Chairman
quote: Your Board is receiving regular updates on the measures being taken by management to deal with the impact of the pandemic on Rolls-Royce. ... Your Board believes that in light of the uncertain macroeconomic outlook this is an appropriate and precautionary measure to take at this point as the group seeks to ensure an appropriate level of liquidity in the event of a prolonged reduction in trading activity.
finding: In the 2020 shock the board acted on precaution and liquidity (withdrawing the final dividend, with R-0779) and monitored management through regular updates.

speaker: Ian Davis, Independent Chairman
quote: While senior management, including the executive team, have accepted a 20% reduction, which is being mirrored by your Board. The remuneration committee meanwhile will make full use of its discretion to amend any future executive awards under the group's long-term incentive plans to avoid any windfall gains caused by general stock market recovery
finding: The Remuneration Committee sets long-term incentive plans and uses discretion to stop executives gaining from a market rebound rather than from performance; directors cut their own fees in the crisis.

speaker: Warren East, CEO
quote: consider it prudent, therefore, to prioritize resilience and flexibility, in particular, taking into account our reasonable worst-case scenario. And as a result, today, we're announcing plans to increase our resilience through the uncertainty with the recapitalization package. ... It's our responsibility to prepare for the reasonable worst case.
finding: The October 2020 recapitalisation (GBP 2bn rights issue, bonds, UKEF-backed loans; with R-0790) was sized to a reasonable worst case, not the base case: the board chose dilution over balance-sheet risk.

speaker: Warren East, CEO
quote: Of course, that's our motivational headwind at the moment and we are looking at how we can design things to be more appropriate. But it is a matter for the remuneration committee and the board.
finding: Incentive targets (an analyst called the LTIP target unachievable after the 2015 warnings) are set by the Remuneration Committee and the board, not by the CEO.

speaker: Tufan Erginbilgic, CEO
quote: But if you really push me, I think I will go for cash because that's effectively the value creation. LTIP, I'm not going to comment on it right now. As you know, we are at the stage that our remuneration policy is expiring. So there is a work that Board leads, obviously, Remuneration Committee leads on the new remuneration policy.
finding: The CEO said in August 2023 that the remuneration policy was expiring and that work on the new one was led by the board and its Remuneration Committee, not by him; asked to choose, he named cash as his preferred measure of value creation.

speaker: Mark Morris, CFO
quote: So again, we're committed to be sure that we have a strong but efficient balance sheet. And what I would say is it's something that we review at the board regularly. So we've announced a GBP 1 billion share buyback.
finding: The board reviews the balance sheet regularly and backed a GBP 1bn buyback in 2014 at a cycle top; it was stopped half-way in July 2015 (R-0547), the first of a decade of cuts to payouts.

speaker: David Smith, CFO
quote: We've also increased our payment to shareholders by another 5%, and that reflects the continued confidence of the board in the future growth of this company.
finding: Pre-crisis, the board kept raising the payout as a confidence signal, months before the 2015-16 cuts.

speaker: Warren East, CEO
quote: we also talked about the fact that the board will be reviewing this. The board will be reviewing it at the normal time and changes, if any, will be announced at that time.
finding: Dividend changes are a board decision taken at the normal reporting points.

speaker: Warren East, CEO
quote: We'll be managing the cash as we go through that period. And we'll be always keeping an eye to other requirements for cash, what's going on with the share price and long-term shareholder value. So it's a decision that will be taken in the round, and the board will be involved every quarter.
finding: Cash and shareholder-payment choices are reviewed by the board every quarter, against other calls on cash and long-term shareholder value.

speaker: Warren East, CEO
quote: And for the time being, our board has decided to hold the dividend where it is.
finding: The board held the reduced dividend flat through the 2017 investment peak.

speaker: Helen McCabe, CFO
quote: particularly where Rolls-Royce has come from a historic perspective that our first priority always after safety is making sure that we have a strong balance sheet, a resilient balance sheet, and we maintain that.
finding: The capital order the CFO presents (safety, then balance sheet) is framed by the company's history of crises. (inference) As the board-approved frame, it puts balance-sheet resilience above growth and distributions.

speaker: Helen McCabe, CFO
quote: And we are pleased to announce that the Board is recommending a cash dividend of 6p per share in respect to the full year 2024, representing a payout ratio of 30% of underlying profit after tax, the first dividend paid by Rolls-Royce in over 5 years
finding: In February 2025 the board recommended the first dividend since 2019 (6p, 30% payout), alongside a GBP 1bn buyback (RX-0102, RX-0247), only after all three agencies rated the company investment grade.

speaker: Helen McCabe, CFO
quote: These measures along with strong operational execution and earnings and cash flow growth should help us achieve a strong investment-grade rating. We have made good progress building balance sheet resilience. And as we continue through transformation, we will remain prudent in our approach to leverage and we will maintain robust liquidity levels.
finding: The 2025 frame targets a strong investment-grade rating, prudent leverage and robust liquidity, even with net cash.

speaker: John Rishton, CEO
quote: We've also announced today our medium-term outlook. We've recently been through that with our board.
finding: Medium-term guidance is reviewed by the board before it is published.

speaker: John Rishton, CEO
quote: those kind of unethical behaviors are completely unacceptable to me, to the board, and we will not tolerate them. We've hired Lord Gold, who's helping us make sure that we have the right policies and procedures in place
finding: Facing concerns over improper business practices in 2014, management said the board would not tolerate unethical behaviour and an outside adviser (Lord Gold) was hired; compliance risk is a board red line.

speaker: Ian Davis, Chairman
quote: Beverly Goulet, most recently as Senior Executive with American Airlines Group joined us in July. We announced 2 months ago the appointment of Nick Luff, Chief Financial Officer of RELX Group, who joins the board from today, subject to shareholder approval.
finding: Two directors still on the board in July 2022 (RG-0001) joined in 2017-18: Beverly Goulet, an airline executive (customer view), and Nick Luff, a sitting FTSE CFO who chaired the Audit Committee from 2020 (RG-0006).
